definitions.explanation: The simplified forms of kanji adopted as standard in Japan after the 1946 postwar script reform. These replaced the more complex {旧字体|きゅうじたい} (old-form kanji) for everyday use.

examples.japanese: 「⟦{学|がく}→〜学：09846_gaku⟧」⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{新字体|しんじたい}だ。
⟦{現在|げんざい}→現在：01556_genzai⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{教育|きょういく}→教育：01313_kyouiku⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{新字体|しんじたい}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{使|つか}われている→使う：00473_tsukau⟧。
examples.english: In current education, new-form kanji are used.

examples.japanese: {新字体|しんじたい}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{画数|かくすう}→画数：13581_kakusuu⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{減|へ}らして→減らす：02414_herasu⟧⟦{書|か}き→書く：00477_kaku⟧やすく⟦した→する：00392_suru⟧もの⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{多|おお}い→多い：01127_ooi⟧。
examples.english: Many new-form kanji were made easier to write by reducing the number of strokes.

notes:
Composed of {新|しん} (new), ⟦{字|じ}→字：01606_ji⟧ (character), and ⟦{体|たい}→体：09872_tai⟧ (form, style). The standard kanji forms used in Japan today. The simplification reduced stroke counts to make reading and writing easier. Not all kanji were simplified — only those deemed overly complex received new forms.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {新字体|しんじたい}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{改|あらた}める→改める：12923_aratameru⟧ — to convert to new-form kanji
- {新字体|しんじたい}⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{旧字体|きゅうじたい}→旧字体：27161_kyuujitai⟧ — new-form and old-form kanji
- {新字体|しんじたい}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{漢字|かんじ}→漢字：09480_kanji⟧ — new-form kanji characters

RELATED WORDS:
- ⟦{旧字体|きゅうじたい}→旧字体：27161_kyuujitai⟧ — old-form kanji; the traditional, more complex forms replaced by {新字体|しんじたい}
- ⟦{常用漢字|じょうようかんじ}→常用漢字：20778_jouyoukanji⟧ — kanji for common use; the official list of kanji approved for everyday use
- ⟦{簡体字|かんたいじ}→簡体字：13894_kantaiji⟧ — simplified Chinese characters; a similar but more extensive simplification used in mainland China

CULTURAL NOTE:
Japan's simplification was more conservative than China's. Many {新字体|しんじたい} are identical to or close to the traditional forms, while Chinese ⟦{簡体字|かんたいじ}→簡体字：13894_kantaiji⟧ often differ drastically.
